narration: India has thirteen million kirana stores.
Only about one in ten keeps its books digitally. The rest run on a notebook.
And one in three customers buys on udhaar — credit, on trust.
Every rupee of it is written by hand, and chased in person.
So I asked: what if the shopkeeper could just say it? Bol-Khata — speak an entry, know before you lend, and let the agent collect.
Ramesh ne paanch sau rupaye udhaar liye. Written to Ramesh Mishra's khata, balance read back.
Every customer has a full khata, with a one-tap WhatsApp reminder.
Payments bring the balance down instantly.
And a new name simply opens a new khata — no forms.
Or just speak. Gnani Prisma turns speech into text, the agent updates the khata, and Gnani Timbre speaks the answer back.
Before lending, ask. Chauhan ji has broken two promises — so Bol-Khata says no.
Sharma ji always pays on time. Yes.
When money is overdue, the agent makes the collections call itself — politely agreeing a date and logging the promise. Here, with a simulated customer.
Gnani Prisma and Timbre for speech, GPT-OSS on Groq for reasoning, and a rule engine guarding every rupee.
Thirteen million counters. Each one can now just speak — no typing, no forgotten udhaar. Bol-Khata: your dukaan, your voice, your digital khata.
